newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Second Palestinian land dealer slain.
newsitem.headline: Second Palestinian land dealer slain.

text.p: Palestinian officials said on Sunday a man who had sold land to Israelis was found shot dead a day earlier but denied their forces were responsible.

Harbi Abu Sarah was the second land dealer found dead in the West Bank since Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen was quoted in a published report as saying that Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.
Washington and an international human rights group have urged Palestinian President Yasser Arafat not to allow retribution against land dealers.

The first dealer killed last week, Farid Bashiti, 70, of Jerusalem, was hurriedly buried on Sunday at a cemetery in the desert between Jerusalem and Jericho. His funeral had been repeatedly postponed and the burial site changed out of fear of violence. Bashiti was found dead in Ramallah.

Abu Sarah, a man in his sixties, was found dead at the village of Tira near the Ramallah self-rule enclave in the West Bank on Saturday and buried in his home village of nearby Ain Yabrud on Sunday, Palestinian sources said.

Israel's Itim news agency quoted a relative of Abu Sarah as saying Palestinian security forces "apparently were involved" in the killing. It quoted other Palestinian sources saying the man was killed in a dispute between families.
The governor of Ramallah, Mustafa Liftawi, said Palestinian forces were not involved in Abu Sarah's death.

"We, the Palestinian Authority and the Palestinian police are not involved in any way in the killing of this man. He was found by people yesterday morning. They called police who took him to Ramallah hospital," Liftawi told Reuters.
"He was killed by a bullet in his ear. In his village he is known as a dealer of land. He sold land to Israelis and he has a bad reputation ethically."

An Israeli court on Thursday ordered the detention of a Palestinian man and a woman on suspicion of involvement in Bashiti's murder. Israel alleged Bashiti, who held Israeli citizenship, was killed for selling land to Jews.

Palestinians say Israelis have been buying land in the West Bank, including Israeli-annexed East Jerusalem, to block a political agreement which they hope will end Israeli rule in the areas captured by the Jewish state in the 1967 Middle East war.
